title: Graphic Packaging Consolidates North American Operations and Centralizes Supply Chain, Appointing Two Executive Vice Presidents

body_markdown:
*D. Keith Hamilton to lead North America Mills & Converting Operations; Adrian Poretti to lead Global Supply Chain & Procurement*


ATLANTA


, Nov. 16, 2026


/PRNewswire/ -- Graphic Packaging Holding Company (NYSE: GPK), a global leader in sustainable consumer packaging, today announced the appointments of D. Keith Hamilton as Executive Vice President, North America Mills & Converting Operations, effective December 1, 2026, and Adrian Poretti as Executive Vice President, Global Supply Chain & Procurement, effective December 14, 2026.


These executive leadership appointments mark the next phase of Graphic Packaging's transformation, aligning the organization to better serve customers, strengthen partnerships and position the company for long-term growth. Hamilton will lead Graphic Packaging's North American mills and converting operations as a combined division to enhance service delivery for the world's leading brands, retailers and QSRs. Poretti will centralize global procurement and establish a streamlined supply chain to drive efficiency and scale benefits.


"Keith and Adrian bring exceptional depth of experience and a track record of turning complex manufacturing and supply chain networks into stronger, more integrated operations," said Robbert Rietbroek, President and Chief Executive Officer at Graphic Packaging. "Keith's packaging expertise and operational discipline, combined with Adrian's global supply chain leadership, will strengthen our ability to serve customers and improve performance. Both are proven developers of talent and the right leaders to help us realize the full potential of our network and accelerate our value creation."


**D. Keith Hamilton to Lead North American Manufacturing Operations**


Hamilton will oversee North American Mills and Converting operations, Engineering, Continuous Improvement and Quality, as well as global Environmental, Health and Safety. He will align production planning and goals across the region to strengthen performance and deliver greater consistency for customers while advancing operational and commercial excellence across the company.


Hamilton brings more than 30 years of leadership experience across the packaging and automotive manufacturing industries as well as the U.S. Navy. Most recently, he served as President of Corrugated Packaging at Georgia-Pacific, overseeing commercial and operating performance. Previously, he led operations for its 40-plant corrugated division, advancing best practices and improving productivity.


Earlier in his career, Hamilton held manufacturing leadership roles at Goodyear and General Motors and served as a nuclear operator in the U.S. Navy. He holds master's degrees in mechanical engineering and management from Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute.


**Adrian Poretti to Lead Global Supply Chain and Procurement**


Poretti will unify the global procurement, planning and logistics functions to coordinate purchasing, production requirements and the movement of materials and finished products. Poretti brings more than 30 years of supply chain and manufacturing experience.


Most recently, he served as Vice President, Global Manufacturing at Ontex, responsible for manufacturing sites across North America and Europe dedicated to fiber-based consumer packaging. Previously, as Chief Supply Chain Officer at Hostess Brands, he integrated supply chain functions to improve product availability, customer service, cost performance and safety.


At Kimberly-Clark, Poretti led North American supply chain operations. He also held global manufacturing and supply chain leadership roles, establishing common standards across regions. He holds an engineering degree from Universidad Católica de Córdoba and an MBA from Universidad del Salvador y Deusto in Argentina.


**Joseph Yost to Retire as Americas Leader**


The company also announced that Joseph Yost, Executive Vice President and President, Americas, will retire effective January 16, 2027. Over nearly four decades with Graphic Packaging and its predecessor companies, Yost has held leadership roles across supply chain, Global Beverage and Europe, served as President, International, and twice led the Americas business.


"Joe has made a lasting contribution to Graphic Packaging through his leadership and commitment to our people and customers," Rietbroek said. "I am grateful for his partnership and the counsel he has provided to set up the company for its next chapter, and I join our colleagues in wishing him the very best in his retirement."


**About Graphic Packaging Holding Company**


Graphic Packaging Holding Company (NYSE: GPK), headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, designs and produces consumer packaging made primarily from renewable or recycled materials. An industry leader in innovation, the Company is committed to reducing the environmental footprint of consumer packaging. Graphic Packaging operates a global network of design and manufacturing facilities serving the world's most widely recognized brands in food, beverage, foodservice, household, and other consumer products.
